newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Qualcomm plans Ukraine telcoms production.
newsitem.headline: Qualcomm plans Ukraine telcoms production.

text.p: Qualcomm Inc. of San Diego plans to begin producing digital telecommunications equipment next year in Ukraine, where only eight million out of 52 million people have telephones.

Chief Executive Irwin Jacobs said late Thursday that Qualcomm had formed a joint venture with local firm Telesystemy Ukrainy to manufacture wireless telephones at a factory in the eastern city of Dnipropetrovsk.
The deal marks the first attempt to bring local wireless communications to Ukraine, formerly part of the Soviet Union.
"We're starting out with investments in the range of $10 million to $20 million," Jacobs said.
However, Qualcomm plans to eventually increase investment to $2 billion, providing the system was accepted by consumers in Ukraine, he said.
He said Qualcomm hoped initially to make 250,000 telephones a year when production begins in mid-1997.
Telesystemy Ukrainy owns 51 percent of the joint venture and Qualcomm 49 percent.
Under Ukrainian law a Ukrainian company must be the majority partner in a telecommunications joint venture.
